thread:
alex_sales: Heads up 0: customer running a POC sees a bunch of partial traces and apparently reused trace ids in their Splunk export after we turned on high-sample logging. They say correlation looks broken.
nina_sre: Do they mean span-less traces (only root) or multiple unrelated requests with same trace id?
alex_sales: The latter. Multiple unrelated requests have identical trace ids in the exported logs. They also saw exporter returning 503 from our egress to their collector a few times.
jon_runtime: 503s + partial traces -> could be backpressure + a truncation bug. We had one runtime bug where we truncated hex trace ids to 8 bytes for legacy compatibility; if their collector expects 16 bytes you can collide.
emma_support: I pulled a raw export file they attached. Example lines:```
{"trace_id":"1a2b3c4d","req":"GET /api/v1/foo","ts":1680000000}
{"trace_id":"1a2b3c4d","req":"POST /api/v1/bar","ts":1680000002}
```
Two different endpoints same short id. Their SDK uses 32-char hex ids normally.
nina_sre: That is consistent with truncation. Where in pipeline do we shorten IDs? Jon?
jon_runtime: We have a legacy path that coerces incoming otel ids into our internal compact form for index keys. There's a faulty fallback that slices the hex string: trace_id = trace_id[:8] when compatibility_mode=true. Shouldn't run for new POC workspaces.
emma_support: Also the 503s were during burstswe see our exporter thread pool saturating and then retries piling up; retry jitter + immediate retry caused duplicate log lines with same truncated id.
jon_runtime: Ok plan: 1) revert compatibility_mode for the POC workspace (safe) 2) add a hotfix to preserve full trace_id length on export 3) temporary backpressure mitigation: lower exporter concurrency and enable exponential backoff with jitter.
alex_sales: Customer will want an ETA and a dashboard showing before/after. They are sensitive to data correctness.
nina_sre: I'll make a dashboard filter for workspace "poc-zenith" showing metrics: export.503_count, export.retry_count, traces.per_missing_spans. Also add a panel for distinct(trace_id) per minute to spot collisions.
jon_runtime: Hotfix patch: set ENV REDWOOD_COMPAT_TRUNCATE_TRACE_IDS=false and REDWOOD_EXPORT_CONCURRENCY=2 and REDWOOD_EXPORT_RETRY_POLICY=exponential_jitter(100,2000,5). For the runtime change I'll push ENG-10234 with a patch to remove the slice fallback.
emma_support: I'll coordinate with customer to pause wide replays until we fix truncation; we can reprocess the problematic window after we ensure full ids are preserved. They want us to re-ingest logs for 2024-03-10 14:00-15:00 UTC.
infra-bot: Deploy started for poc-zenith/sandbox rollback commit=9c4e2 (alex)
infra-bot: Deploy succeeded in 1m40s
jon_runtime: Hotfix merged and deployed to sandbox. Verified exported lines now show 32-char ids:```
{"trace_id":"1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e2f3a4b5c6d","req":"GET /api/v1/foo","ts":1680000000}
```
No collisions on a quick diff.
nina_sre: Dashboard link: Console -> Observability -> Dashboards -> "POC Zen - export health". I added panels and shared with customer.
emma_support: Customer confirmed collisions disappeared in new exports and 503s stopped after we lowered concurrency. They authorized reprocess for the 1h window.
jon_runtime: I'll kick off reprocess job with dedupe safety: reprocess will only upsert traces that are missing root/span counts, avoiding duplicates. Job id: reprocess-786.
alex_sales: I'll update the customer and include the dashboard link + reprocess job id. Thanks all for rapid help. :rocket:
nina_sre: Follow-up: create a runtime test to assert trace_id length is 32 hex chars on export and add regression test in CI. Filed SRE-211.
jon_runtime: Filed ENG-10234 (remove truncate) and ENG-10270 (add export trace id length check).
emma_support: Closing loop with customer now. If anything flares, reopen. :thumbsup:
